title: Vote explanations must demonstrate understanding of the proposal, not merely state a position
content:
A.1.6.2.2 requires Aligned Delegates to "provide substantive reasoning when explaining their votes," and specifies three cumulative requirements for a compliant explanation: it must "demonstrate understanding of the proposal's core mechanisms or changes," "articulate a reasoned basis for the vote position," and "address at least one substantive aspect of the proposal (benefits, risks, implementation, or alignment with ecosystem goals)." Explanations are due "within one (1) week of the end of the voting period."

The first criterion is the demanding one and the reason this is not boilerplate. Requiring a *reasoned basis* alone would be satisfied by any coherent sentence; requiring demonstrated understanding of the mechanism makes the explanation a check on whether the delegate actually read and comprehended what they voted on. A delegate voting by heuristic, by following another delegate, or by instruction cannot easily fake it.

This is the mechanism that makes delegation legible to the SKY holders who supply the voting power. They cannot observe a delegate's reasoning directly, and under the anonymity regime they cannot know who the delegate is; a mandatory, timely, substantive written record is the only available proxy for whether their power is being exercised thoughtfully.

The post-hoc deadline is a deliberate choice with a trade-off. Explanations after the voting period closes cannot inform other voters or be coordinated around before the outcome, which protects against delegates cueing each other — but it also means the reasoning arrives too late to be debated when it would matter. The Atlas is optimizing for accountability and independence rather than deliberation.

Because failures here are Tier 1 procedural breaches, and A.1.6.1.4.1 makes any Tier 1 breach terminal during the 90-day probation, a new delegate who writes a thin explanation can lose the role for it.
description: A.1.6.2.2 sets three cumulative content tests — grasp of core mechanisms, a reasoned basis, and engagement with a substantive aspect — due within one week of the voting period ending.
